## Goal

**As** a project owner scaffolding agent guidance from this repository, **I want** `templates/project-AGENTS.md` to carry the project-level conventions that audits actually enforce, **so that** a new project inherits the two rules that a 2026-10-29 cross-project audit session had to invent on the spot instead of discovering them late.

Discovered-from: `WL-0MVR8EXR6009F05V` (ContextHub) — an epic audit that returned `Ready to close: No` on an acceptance criterion the producer had already decided to accept, and an `implement` run whose push gate did not run the suite the skill documentation says it runs.

## Scope note (read before implementing)

The definite "the template" is taken to mean **`templates/project-AGENTS.md`** — the canonical project `AGENTS.md` seed consumed by `scripts/init_project_agents.py` (see `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md`). That file is deliberately minimal ("reference structure only"), so this item **adds project-level guidance sections, not a copy of the global rules**.

If the intent was instead the framework sources (`skill/audit`, `skill/report`, `skill/implement`) rather than the project template, re-scope this item before implementing — the framework findings are listed at the end as separate, unfiled work.

## Problem

Two conventions were needed during the ContextHub epic and neither is documented for a project owner:

1. **Recording a producer-accepted acceptance-criteria variance.** The producer decided to accept one AC without the last piece of live evidence. The audit runner ignores `wl auditWaiver` entirely (`grep -n waiver skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` → no matches); the *only* way to make an audit score that criterion `adjusted` (non-blocking) instead of `partial` (blocking) is to write the accepted variance into the criterion's own text in the work-item description, resolve the recorded open question, and *additionally* record `wl audit-waive` so the closure guard and `wl doctor audit-gaps` agree. Done that way, the epic audit returned `Ready to close: Yes` with the criterion `adjusted`, a clean Phase 1/Phase 2 (`calls=2 parse_ok=2`). Done any other way it silently stays blocking and the item ping-pongs between implement and audit.
2. **Declaring the project's real push gate.** `skill/implement` and `skill/audit` both state that the dev-push pre-push hook enforces the full suite (`run_tests.py --scope full`). That is true only where the v3 hook is installed: this repository ships `.githooks/pre-push` (v3, with the scope-aware test gate), but a project seeded earlier (ContextHub) still runs `worklog:pre-push-hook:v2`, which enforces branch policy, the context budget and worklog sync **and nothing else**. Green test evidence therefore came from the `implement.py finish` full-scope run, not the hook. A project owner needs to be told to assert this, because the failure mode is silent: pushes succeed and the cached full-suite evidence the audit consumes read-only never exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `templates/project-AGENTS.md` gains a `## Recording an accepted acceptance-criteria variance` section stating the three-step procedure — (a) amend the criterion's text in the work-item description with an explicit "Accepted variance (producer decision, <date>)" clause naming what evidence stands in for the missing evidence, (b) resolve the corresponding open question in the item description, (c) record `wl audit-waive <id> --reason "<why>"` — and explains **why** the description is mandatory (the audit runner scores an AC from its text and ignores `auditWaiver`).
- AC2: The same template gains a `## Declaring your push gate` section telling a project owner to verify which pre-push hook version the project actually runs (`git config core.hooksPath` + the `worklog:pre-push-hook:vN` banner line) and to record the answer in the project's own guidance, so the full-suite evidence an audit consumes is known to exist (or is known to come from `implement.py finish` instead of the hook).
- AC3: `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md` is updated to match — it must describe the template as carrying these two optional guidance sections and stay truthful about the "reference structure only, never a copy of the global rules" constraint; `scripts/init_project_agents.py` output must remain idempotent (re-running never duplicates the reference or the new sections).
- AC4: A test pins the guarantee: emitting a fresh project `AGENTS.md` via `scripts/init_project_agents.py` produces a file containing both new sections, and re-running it is a no-op (`scripts/init_project_agents.py --dry-run --json` reports no change).
- AC5: The two conventions stay project-scoped: no global workflow rule is duplicated into the template (the global layer remains `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` via `scripts/install_pi.sh`), and `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` is re-measured only if the template changes the always-loaded surface.
- AC6: Full project test suite passes with the new changes (enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Key Files

- `templates/project-AGENTS.md` — the canonical project `AGENTS.md` seed; the two new sections go here.
- `scripts/init_project_agents.py` — the installer that reads the template (`TEMPLATE_PATH`) and must stay idempotent.
- `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md` — the installer documentation to keep in sync (it quotes the canonical file verbatim, so the quoted block must be updated too).
- `tests/` — wherever the installer's tests live (`grep -rln "init_project_agents" tests/`), for the AC4 pin.

## Constraints

- Do **not** copy global agent rules (workflow, wl lifecycle, coding disciplines) into the template — that duplication was removed by `SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G` and must not come back.
- Project-specific guidance stays project-specific: both new sections are conventions a *project owner* opts into, not new global mandates.
- Keep the installer idempotent and its output deterministic; no new dependency.
- UK English; match the existing Markdown style of the file and its quoted copy in the docs.

## Related findings from the same session (not in this item's scope — file separately if wanted)

1. `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` maps an AC verdict of `adjusted` to `unmet` in its Acceptance Criteria table (it only knows `met`/`unmet`), so a *passing* audit that carries an accepted variance renders as `❌ failed` with an `unmet` row. The report had to be corrected by hand.
2. `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py start` fails (`ERROR: Failed to create worktree …`) when a feature branch with the expected name still exists but its worktree directory was removed; the operator has to `git worktree add <path> <branch>` manually and re-run `start` (which then resumes idempotently).
3. `skill/audit` in-main-slot mode (default) emits `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` child screens that, when unserviced, produce a `Ready to close: No` whose AC rows are all `partial` **and** persist partial child audits that later block the parent — `--no-child-in-main-slot` was the only path that produced a usable report in three consecutive runs.
data.title: Carry the accepted-variance and push-gate conventions into templates/project-AGENTS.md

# implement.py start: nested node_modules symlink blocks submodule init (bootstrap ordering)

**Discovered from:** RISE-0MVRZKINX004HNEE (tce-the-rising implement run, 2026-10-29).

## Problem

`implement.py start` initialises submodules *after* it creates the
`node_modules` symlinks. When a submodule's own root has a `node_modules` in
the main checkout (tce-the-rising's `core` submodule does), the nested-symlink
pass creates `<worktree>/core/node_modules` inside the still-**empty**
submodule directory. `git submodule update --init` then cannot clone into
`core/` and fails:

```
fatal: clone of 'file:///home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine' into submodule path '…/core' failed
fatal: destination path '…/core' already exists and is not an empty directory.
```

Because submodule init failures are deliberately fail-open (SA-0MSN52GGN002B0AZ
AC2), `start` only logs a warning and the session proceeds with an
**uninitialised submodule**: `npm run build` (`tsc --noEmit`) then dies with
`Cannot find module './core/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin'`,
`@core-engine/SaveLoad`, etc. Every child session in that worktree must
hand-fix the checkout before it can build.

Secondary defect: even after a successful init, the symlink is not ignored by
the submodule's `.gitignore` (`node_modules/` has a trailing slash, which does
not match a *symlink*), so the superproject reports `M core` and the worktree
looks dirty.

## Evidence

- Call order in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (start phase):
  `_ensure_node_modules_symlink` (≈L4608) → `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`
  (≈L4614) → `_ensure_submodules` (≈L4618).
- Observed on tce-the-rising worktree
  `wl-RISE-0MVRZKINX004HNEE-…`: `git submodule status` showed
  `-19f30ac… core` (uninitialised) while `core/` contained only the
  `node_modules` symlink; the first `npm run build` produced ~40 `TS2307`
  errors from the missing submodule.
- Manual fix that worked: `rm core/node_modules && rmdir core`,
  `git -c protocol.file.allow=always submodule update --init --recursive`,
  re-create `core/node_modules`, and add `node_modules` to the submodule's
  `info/exclude` (the trailing-slash pattern in `core/.gitignore` does not
  match the symlink).

## Required change

- Run `_ensure_submodules` **before** the node_modules symlink passes, or make
  the nested-symlink pass skip paths that are inside an
  uninitialised/unchecked-out submodule (a gitlink with an empty directory).
- Make the worktree's `git status` clean after the symlinks are created: drop
  or neutralise the symlink's untracked status (e.g. immediately cover it by
  an exclude entry, or create the nested link only after init and add the
  path to the worktree's exclude).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A worktree whose submodule root has a `node_modules` in the main checkout is
  fully initialised by `start`: `git submodule status` in the worktree shows a
  checked-out submodule (no leading `-`) and the repo's build succeeds.
- Ordering regression test: fixture repo with a local-path submodule plus a
  `<submodule>/node_modules` in the main checkout → after `start`, the
  submodule is checked out at the recorded commit and the worktree
  `git status --porcelain` is clean.
- The fail-open contract is unchanged: a genuinely failing
  `git submodule update` still only logs a warning and does not abort `start`.
- No behavioural change for repos without submodules or without a submodule
  `node_modules`.
- `implement/SKILL.md` submodule section notes the ordering constraint.

## Constraints

- Do not remove the node_modules symlinking feature itself
  (SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B) — only fix its ordering/ignoring relative to
  submodules.
- Keep the change generic; no tce-the-rising / `core`-specific hardcoding.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_ensure_submodules`,
  `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`, start-phase call order.
- `skill/implement/tests/` — ordering/regression test next to
  `test_implement_submodules.py`-style fixtures.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — submodule documentation.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B** – Auto-symlink node_modules into implement worktrees (implement.py start) (completed)
- **SA-0MVPI400Y001FOM1** – Worktree-local node_modules link farm (completed)
- **SA-0MVB71260006J3FY** – Migrate implement.py repo/worktree fixtures to git_sandbox (blocked)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0msgs763c006sm1b, 0msn52ggn002b0az, abort, ac2, acceptance (+157 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0msgs763c006sm1b, 0msn52ggn002b0az, abort, ac2, acceptance (+152 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0msgs763c006sm1b, abort, ac2, acceptance, add (+150 more)
data.title: implement.py start: nested node_modules symlink blocks submodule init (bootstrap ordering)

## Goal

As an agent running the changed-scope test gate, I want a changed `tests/unit/test-*.mjs` file to select the node suite for that directory, so a JS/TS test edit is actually executed before commit instead of only at the push-time full suite.

## Problem

`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_is_test_file()` recognises `test_*.py`, `*_test.py`, `*.test.mjs` and `*_test.mjs` but **not** the repo's dominant node convention `test-*.mjs`. Consequences:

1. A changed `tests/unit/test-*.mjs` file is not classified as a test file, so `map_changed_to_tests()` tries the convention mapping instead (`test_<stem>.py` etc.) and selects nothing.
2. The same filter builds the `all_tests` pool used by import-graph expansion, so `test-*.mjs` files can never be selected there either.
3. Emission of a node command requires a selected `.mjs` path, so no `node --test` command is produced at all.

Verified while delivering SA-0MVTU1WHS002HN1C: editing three test files (`skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py`, `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`, `tests/unit/test-check-final-validation.mjs`) produced a changed-scope command containing only `pytest ...` — no `node --test`. 46 of the 47 `tests/unit/*.mjs` files use the `test-` prefix, so the gap covers almost the whole node unit suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `_is_test_file()` recognises `test-*.mjs` (and the equivalent `test-*.js`/`test-*.ts` naming) as test files.
- A unit test asserts that changing a `tests/unit/test-foo.mjs` file selects `tests/unit/test-foo.mjs` and causes a `node --test` command to be emitted by the changed-scope command builder (no pytest-only command).
- The selection never invents a path that does not exist (the existing LP-0MTZYRTNF0092JKW existence filter still applies).
- Existing changed-scope selection tests stay green; the full suite stays green.

## Constraints

- Do not widen selection to arbitrary `.mjs` helper files (e.g. `cli-helpers.mjs`); only the test-file naming conventions.
- Keep the single-source-of-truth rule: one filter function, no duplicated naming logic.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py`

## Related work

- discovered-from:SA-0MVTU1WHS002HN1C (observed while adding hermetic ship-gate tests).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MRIIQLQI001RQVB** – Refactor command/doc.md for conciseness (completed)
- **SA-0MRMB6P6M008H4U4** – Fix legacy skill/ path reference in planall SKILL.md (completed)
- **SA-0MSHZ08OY005EE7W** – Delete AMPA installer/plugin test artifacts (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: acceptance, actually, agent, already, applies (+99 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0mtzyrtnf0092jkw, acceptance, actually, agent, already (+98 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: acceptance, actually, adding, agent, already (+96 more)
data.title: Changed-scope test selection ignores test-*.mjs node suites

# Refactor skill: never inject marker blocks above a shebang or encoding line

**Headline:** After the shebang fix (SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F) the refactor skill
still prepends its marker block above a PEP 263 encoding line and above a
Python module docstring, so annotated files implicitly change the file
encoding cookie position that the interpreter reads and trample the module
docstring convention. It also rewrites files without preserving line endings.
The remaining fix: compute an insertion offset from the file head (shebang,
then coding line, then optional module docstring) and splice the marker
block *below* all of them, writing with `newline=""`.

## Problem statement

`skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` places the REFACTOR marker block at the
top of the file and only steps past a leading shebang. Two Python-specific
file-head constructs are still displaced:

1. A **PEP 263 encoding declaration** (`# -*- coding: ... -*-`, or
   `# coding: ...`). PEP 263 requires the cookie on line 1, or line 2 when
   line 1 is a shebang. Prepending the marker pushes the cookie to line 3+,
   so Python no longer honours it — an encoding regression on files the skill
   touched. This gap was explicitly deferred by SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F (its
   "Open Questions" section records the cookie, out of scope there).
2. A **module docstring**. Prepending the marker above a leading module
   docstring splits the docstring from the module head; it also breaks the
   convention that the docstring is the first statement, and produces a
   noisier diff. AC1 therefore places the marker after the docstring too.

A third defect: the file is written with `open(..., "w")` and default line
handling, which can normalise line endings (CRLF → LF) — AC3 requires writing
with `newline=""` so line endings and trailing-newline state are preserved.

Leaving these unhandled means the skill keeps creating preventable lint
findings and file mutations on annotated scripts.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `/skill:refactor` or the implement
  pipeline's refactor step — they inherit preventable file-head mutations and
  encoding-changes on files the skill touched.
- **Producers triaging the refactor backlog** — self-inflicted findings
  consume triage and implementation capacity.
- **Developers** — annotated scripts must keep a valid encoding declaration
  (when present) and a clean module head.

User stories:

- As an agent running the refactor step, I want the marker block inserted
  *after* any shebang, encoding line, and module docstring, so annotated
  Python files keep their interpreter directive on line 1, their encoding
  cookie where the interpreter reads it, and their docstring as the first
  statement.
- As a maintainer, I want files the skill annotates to remain byte-stable
  apart from the marker (no line-ending normalisation), so diffs are minimal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `inject_refactor_comment()` inserts its block *after* any shebang
      (`#!…`) and any PEP 263 coding line, and after a Python module docstring
      when the file opens with one; on files with none of these the block
      still goes to the top as today.
- [ ] Markdown/HTML block-style markers (`<!-- … -->`) keep their current
      placement behaviour, except that a leading shebang or coding line in a
      non-Markdown file is never displaced.
- [ ] Line endings and trailing newline state are preserved (write with
      `newline=""`), so the fix does not normalise CRLF files.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` cover: a file
      starting with a shebang, a file with shebang + coding line, a file with
      shebang + docstring, a plain Python file with no shebang, and a Markdown
      file — each asserting shebang stays on line 1.
- [ ] A regression test asserts that running the repository's lint gate over a
      file annotated by the skill reports no `EXE005`/`EXE001`-style executable
      findings.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` (the "REFACTOR Comments"
      section), and any relevant docs entries.

## Impact

Agents and producers no longer see self-inflicted encoding/executable-bit
findings or docstring trampling on files the refactor skill annotates; every
annotated script keeps its shebang, encoding declaration, and module docstring
exactly where the interpreter and tools expect them.

## Constraints

- Do **not** change marker syntax, the duplicate-suppression match on smell
  type, or `get_comment_style()` file-type mapping — placement only.
- Removal of stale markers on work-item close is **out of scope**; that is
  `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9`.
- Keep the change confined to `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` and its
  tests (plus the SKILL.md/docs wording noted in the last AC).

## Existing state

Since SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F, `inject_refactor_comment()` steps past a leading
shebang via `_split_leading_shebang()` and splices the block immediately
below it (dropping the block's own leading newline). The remaining gaps:

```python
# skill/refactor/comment_injection.py
    shebang, body = _split_leading_shebang(original_content)
    if shebang:
        new_content = shebang + comment_block.lstrip("
") + body
    else:
        new_content = comment_block + original_content   # still displaces
                                                         # coding line / docstring

    with open(file_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:    # no newline=""
        f.write(new_content)
```

- A file opening with `# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-` (no shebang) gets the marker
  above the cookie — the cookie then sits at line 2+, which PEP 263 only
  allows when line 1 is a shebang.
- A file opening with a module docstring gets the marker above it.
- The write path does not preserve line endings (no `newline=""`).
- Field evidence: on 2026-10-30 the implement pipeline's refactor step
  annotated `src/rss_server.py` in the ContentCreator project, pushing
  `#!/usr/bin/env python3` from line 1 to line 13 and producing
  `EXE005 Shebang should be at the beginning of the file`. The finding was
  filed as `OSL-0MVVE7V84007DQD0`, implemented as removing the skill's own
  marker, and pinned with `tests/test_rss_script_entrypoint.py`.

## Desired change

`inject_refactor_comment()` computes an insertion offset from the file head
(shebang, then coding line, then optional module docstring) and splices the
block there, leaving the file head byte-identical otherwise. Extend the
shebang-only helper into a general file-head skipper:

- Step past a leading `#!` line (existing behaviour, preserved).
- Step past a PEP 263 encoding declaration on line 1 (no shebang) or line 2
  (after a shebang) — Python-only concern; the marker belongs below the
  cookie, wherever it sits.
- Step past a leading Python module docstring (a triple-quoted string that
  opens the file body and terminates before the first statement). Heuristic:
  match only a leading `"""…"""`/`'''…'''` that closes before any statement;
  fall back to top-of-file placement when parsing is ambiguous
  (see Risks).
- Write the result with `newline=""` so CRLF and trailing-newline state are
  preserved.

Note for the implementer: with docstring placement the marker moves below
the docstring, so the current `TestShebangPreservation` case that asserts
marker-before-docstring (`content.index("REFACTOR") <
content.index('"""Docstring."""')`) must be updated to assert
marker-after-docstring per AC1. `has_existing_comment()` scans the whole
file, so markers below the docstring are still detected (idempotence
holds).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` — generalise the file-head skip
  (shebang → coding line → docstring); write with `newline=""`
- `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` — placement tests for the
  shebang / coding-line / docstring / Markdown cases; update the affected
  shebang+docstring assertion
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — state the placement rule in the "REFACTOR
  Comments" section
- `docs/refactor.md` — add the placement rule to the comment-injection
  documentation (if a suitable section exists)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** a marker placed after the module docstring is still found by
  `has_existing_comment()`, which scans the whole file rather than the head.
- **Risk (low):** docstring detection is heuristic; an over-eager match could
  move the marker into the middle of code. Mitigation: match only a leading
  triple-quoted string that terminates before the first statement, and fall
  back to top-of-file placement when parsing is ambiguous.
- **Risk (low):** mis-detecting a leading `"…"`/`'…'` string literal as a
  docstring would displace the marker. Constrain detection to triple-quoted
  strings and, where practical, to files whose extension maps to the `.py`
  style.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a general "annotation lifecycle" refactor (placement,
  removal, sweep) is tempting. Record such work against
  `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9`/`SA-0MVZA21600087VRD` instead of widening this item.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F` (completed) — fixed shebang displacement only; its
  deferred PEP 263 cookie question is this item's core scope. Partial overlap
  (shebang placement already shipped) — this item addresses the gaps.
- `SA-0MVGKMNEQ009RZKD` (open) — refactor-skill file-size detection; adjacent
  refactor-skill concern, distinct from comment placement (mutually linked).
- `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9` — remove stale `REFACTOR-` markers when their work
  item closes (marker lifecycle; complements, does not overlap).
- `SA-0MVZA21600087VRD` — reap `REFACTOR-` marker blocks when the recorded
  smell is fixed (marker lifecycle; complements, does not overlap).
- `SA-0MWFW1ZDT006VYM4` (blocked) — implement: unified parser and
  `remove_refactor_marker()` (marker lifecycle; complements, does not overlap).
- `SA-0MWFW1YQ8007E2CZ` (open) — test: REFACTOR marker removal API (marker
  lifecycle; complements, does not overlap).
- `OSL-0MVVE7V84007DQD0` — the ContentCreator item that this defect created
  (fixed by deleting the marker and pinning the entrypoint contract).
- `OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW` — the ContentCreator sweep of stale markers left in
  tests and scripts.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were required: the work item description and the
  completed predecessor (SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F, whose scope notes explicitly
  deferred the encoding-cookie question) fully specify the gap, and the
  related-work search found no duplicate or overlapping open item. Recorded
  here for auditability.
  - Research: inspected `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` (shebang
    handled; coding line, docstring, and `newline=""` unhandled),
    `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` (shebang tests present;
    one assertion contradicts the new docstring AC and must be updated),
    `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` "REFACTOR Comments" section (placement rule
    absent), and ran `wl search` duplicate checks (no full duplicate; partial
    overlap with completed SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F only).
data.title: Refactor skill: never inject marker blocks above a shebang or encoding line

# Pre-commit hook guard sandbox tests

## Goal

As the implementer of the commit-time guard, I want a hermetic test that pins
exactly when `.githooks/pre-commit` must refuse and when it must stay silent, so
the guard can never regress into blocking legitimate work.

Test-first half of parent AC3. This item writes **tests only** — the hook itself
is the sibling item *Pre-commit hook refuses main-checkout dev commits*.

## Context

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` is the sanctioned sandbox: `fixture_git_env()`,
  `scrub_repository_overrides()`, `run_git()`. It strips inherited `GIT_*`
  overrides so a polluted session environment cannot leak into the fixture.
- `tests/test_githooks_portability.py` is the precedent for a throw-away repo
  built from the committed `.githooks/` with `core.hooksPath=.githooks`.
- `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` is the precedent for asserting the
  `scripts/install_pi.sh` wiring block itself.
- The guard target is narrow: **`dev` in the main checkout**. A linked worktree,
  a feature branch, `git merge --ff-only` and a `wl sync` commit must all pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new hermetic module `tests/test_pre_commit_main_checkout_guard.py` builds a
  throw-away repository from the committed `.githooks/` with
  `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, a bare local `origin` and a sandboxed `$HOME`; it
  never touches the real checkout, the real `$HOME` or the network.
- It asserts a commit on `dev` in the main checkout is **refused at commit time**:
  non-zero exit, `HEAD` unchanged, no new commit object, and the refusal message
  names the branch (`dev`), the main checkout path, the worktree requirement and
  the operator override.
- Zero-width proof: after the refused commit attempt the repository's commit
  count and `git rev-parse HEAD` are byte-identical to the pre-attempt values.
- It asserts the hook does **not** fire (exit 0, commit created) when:
  (a) the same commit runs inside a linked worktree (`git worktree add`);
  (b) the main checkout is on a feature branch;
  (c) `ALLOW_MAIN_CHECKOUT_DEV_COMMIT=1` is set (and the override announces
  itself on stderr so a deliberate hot-fix stays auditable).
- It asserts the two legitimate main-checkout movements still succeed: a
  `git merge --ff-only` fast-forward of `dev` (no commit object is created) and a
  `wl sync`-style commit performed inside a temporary linked worktree
  (`.worklog/tmp-worktree-*`, detached `HEAD`) — the shape
  `ContextHub/dist/sync/worktree.js::withTempWorktree` uses.
- The suite is environment-clean: the fixture uses `fixture_git_env()` /
  `scrub_repository_overrides()` so inherited `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` or
  `GIT_WORK_TREE` cannot influence a verdict.
- Tests are run only through the test skill (`run_tests.py`), never ad hoc; the
  new module passes once the hook item lands, and is red before it (the hook
  does not exist yet).

## Minimal implementation

- One test module, module-level docstring citing parent AC3 and the four
  negative cases, helper functions for "make a repo", "commit a file", "add a
  linked worktree".
- No production code, no changes to `.githooks/`, no changes to
  `scripts/install_pi.sh`.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_pre_commit_main_checkout_guard.py` (new)
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (reused)
- `tests/test_githooks_portability.py` (pattern to reuse)

## Dependencies

- None. Must be merged before *Pre-commit hook refuses main-checkout dev commits*.

## Deliverables

- The failing-first test module and a short note on the red→green transition.

# Commit-helper guard tests for audit and code-review

## Goal

As a producer, I want the three skill commit helpers pinned by hermetic tests, so
"refuse to commit on `dev` in the main checkout" cannot be silently dropped from
one of them — especially from the duplicate `skill/code_review/` directory.

Test-first half of parent AC1. Tests only; the hardening is the sibling items
*Shared main-checkout commit guard + audit hardening* and *Harden code-review
commit helper in both directories*.

## Context

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_commit_config_remediation` (≈14222)
  stages one config file and commits with `REMEDIATION_COMMIT_MESSAGE`, locally,
  no push. Returns the short sha or `None`; its call site (≈14439) records
  failures into `results["chore_failures"]`.
- `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py::_commit_changes` (≈425) and the
  duplicate `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` (≈641) run `git add .`
  + `git commit -m "Auto-fix: <linter> applied fixes"`. Both directories are
  live: `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` and
  `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` import `code_review`; `code-review` is
  the skill-facing package that owns `SKILL.md`.
- The shared detection verdict must agree with `.githooks/pre-commit`:
  main checkout ⟺ `git rev-parse --git-dir` == `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`;
  target branch ⟺ `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` == `dev`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Hermetic tests (built on `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`) cover
  `_commit_config_remediation` and `_commit_changes` in both code-review
  directories.
- Refusal case: on `dev` in the main checkout the helper makes **no commit** and
  leaves **no staged change** behind (the staging step never runs), and returns
  its failure sentinel (`None` / `False`).
- Positive cases preserved: in a linked worktree, and on a feature branch in the
  main checkout, each helper still commits a real change — pinned for both.
- `ALLOW_MAIN_CHECKOUT_DEV_COMMIT=1` makes every helper commit (consistent with
  the hook), and the override is logged so the deliberate act is traceable.
- Audit call site: a refusal is recorded in `results["chore_failures"]` with a
  message naming the worktree requirement and the work-item id, so the audit
  report states why the remediation was not committed — it is never silently
  dropped.
- The two code-review helper twins are parametrised in one test so they cannot
  drift apart again; an explicit assertion pins "both directories refuse
  identically".
- Unit tests for the new `skill/shared/commit_guard.py` detection helper
  (`is_main_checkout`, `current_branch`, `commit_refusal_reason`) cover the
  main-checkout, linked-worktree, feature-branch, detached-`HEAD` and override
  cases — so a shell and a Python verdict can never disagree.

## Minimal implementation

- One audit test module, one parametrised code-review test module, and one
  helper-unit test module (or a single module with three test classes).
- No production-code edits.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/tests/` (new module for `_commit_config_remediation`)
- `skill/code-review/tests/` and/or `skill/code_review/tests/` (new parametrised module)
- `skill/shared/tests/` (new `test_commit_guard.py`)
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (reused)

## Dependencies

- None. Must be merged before the two hardening items.

## Deliverables

- Red-first tests for all three helpers plus the shared guard primitive.
data.title: Commit-helper guard tests for audit and code-review

# Start refusal attribution tests

## Goal

As a producer, when `implement.py start` refuses because `dev` is not a pushed
tip, I want the refusal pinned by tests that name the owning work items, so
reconciliation is one step instead of a manual log trawl.

Test-first half of parent AC2. Tests only; the implementation is the sibling item
*Start refusal names owning work items*.

## Context

- `_resolve_start_base` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` ≈8021) produces
  `reason: local_dev_not_a_pushed_tip` and an opaque three-step warning
  (≈8123-8137). `phase_start` (≈12081-12110) posts a work-item comment naming
  only the two tips, then releases the claim to `open`.
- `WORK_ITEM_ID_RE = re.compile(r"\b([A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,9}-[A-Z0-9]{2,})\b")` at
  `implement.py` ≈1951 is the existing id pattern — reuse it, do not add a
  second one.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_start_base_resolution.py` already has
  `test_base_refuses_local_dev_with_unpushed_commits` (≈112) and
  `test_phase_start_refuses_a_worktree_from_unpushed_local_dev` (≈315); extend
  that module rather than starting a new one.
- Related work: SA-0MVY4SG8O001RSQF (open) establishes that commit **body**
  mentions are not ownership evidence — AC2 says *subject scan*, so ownership is
  resolved from the subject only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `skill/implement/tests/test_start_base_resolution.py` gains tests asserting the
  refusal names the owning work item(s) for commits whose **subject** contains an
  id (e.g. `fix: Wrap implicit string concatenation (SA-0MWDKRD8G008Z164)`).
- A commit with no id in its subject is reported as **unattributed** — never
  dropped and never silently attributed to the current work item.
- An id present only in the commit **body** does not make that item the owner
  (subject-scan-only contract, consistent with SA-0MVY4SG8O001RSQF).
- The report carries the attribution machine-readably (per-commit sha, subject,
  owning ids and an `unattributed` flag) under
  `report["steps"]["worktree_base"]`, so `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh` and
  future tooling do not have to re-parse prose.
- The `phase_start` work-item comment names the owning items, keeps the existing
  three-step remedy (inspect, verify, push or reset with operator confirmation)
  and points at the reconciliation helper.
- The refusal decision itself is unchanged: `worktree_refused is True`, no
  worktree created, claim released to `open` — the pushed-tip invariant stays
  exactly as it is.
- Fail-open coverage: an unreachable remote (fetch failure) still branches from
  local `dev`; attribution absence never turns a legitimate start into a refusal.
- Message bound: a long unpushed range is truncated with an explicit
  "… and N more" so the warning stays readable, and that truncation is tested.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend the existing module with attribution-specific tests and a helper that
  builds a repo with 3 unpushed commits (attributed, unattributed, body-only id).
- No production-code edits.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/tests/test_start_base_resolution.py` (extend)

## Dependencies

- None. Must be merged before *Start refusal names owning work items*.

## Deliverables

- Red-first attribution tests.

# Reconcile unpushed dev helper tests

## Goal

As a producer, I want the reconciliation helper's contract pinned by tests —
push by default, reset only on explicit confirmation — so recovery from a
poisoned `dev` can never destroy work by accident.

Test-first half of parent AC4. Tests only; the script and its documentation are
the sibling item *Reconcile unpushed dev helper script and docs*.

## Context

- The helper will live at `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh` and is documented
  in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (pushed-tip guarantees section,
  ≈2638).
- Existing precedents for testing a repository script hermetically:
  `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py`, `tests/test_cleanup_scripts.py`, and
  the sandbox helpers in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`.
- Push policy: pushes go to `dev` only — never `main`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `tests/test_reconcile_unpushed_dev.py` builds a bare local `origin` plus
  a clone whose `dev` carries unpushed commits; no real checkout, `$HOME` or
  network is touched.
- Listing: output names each `origin/dev..dev` commit (short sha + subject) and
  its owning work item(s) parsed from the subject, with an explicit
  **unattributed** bucket.
- Default action is **push**: after a plain run, `origin/dev` advanced and local
  `dev` equals `origin/dev`.
- Reset is opt-in only: without the explicit confirmation flag the helper refuses,
  mutates nothing (both refs byte-identical) and names the flag; with it, the
  helper prints the commits it discards **before** discarding, then resets so
  local `dev` equals `origin/dev`.
- No-op path: when `dev` == `origin/dev` the helper exits 0 with a clear "nothing
  to reconcile" message and mutates nothing.
- `--dry-run` lists and mutates nothing; `--json` emits a machine-readable
  document (commits, owning items, unattributed) stable enough for automation.
- Safety refusals: running in a linked worktree or with `dev` not checked out is
  refused with an actionable message (the helper targets the main checkout).
- Failure safety: a failed push leaves local `dev` unchanged and exits non-zero.

## Minimal implementation

- One hermetic test module driving the script through `subprocess` with a
  sandboxed environment and a local bare remote.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_reconcile_unpushed_dev.py` (new)
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (reused)

## Dependencies

- None. Must be merged before *Reconcile unpushed dev helper script and docs*.

## Deliverables

- Red-first tests for the reconciliation helper.

# Refactor skill injects finding comments into whatever checkout it runs in

## Problem

Discovered during intake of SA-0MWM8XZNI0028SRU (downtime workers commit directly
to `dev` in the main checkout).

The refactor skill writes `<!-- REFACTOR-<item-id> -->` markers directly into
source files in its current working directory. When a downtime-dispatched session
runs it with `--cwd <main checkout root>`, it dirties the shared main checkout
without committing anything.

Observed 2026-11-18 ~16:08-16:12 during a concurrent refactor session: the main
checkout was dirtied with `<!-- REFACTOR-SA-… -->` injections in
`scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`, `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py`,
`skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/config.py`,
`skill/implement/tests/test_cleanup_worktree_action.py` and
`skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py` (plus
`.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`).

This is a **second main-checkout mutation surface** distinct from the
direct-commit path tracked in SA-0MWM8XZNI0028SRU: refactor does not commit, but
a dirty checkout `gate-refused` a concurrent pre-push (the same class of damage —
it blocks other sessions' pushes and worktree creation).

## Relation to the parent item

- Parent SA-0MWM8XZNI0028SRU covers **commits** on `dev` in the main checkout
  (skill commit helpers, the `.githooks/pre-commit` guard, `start` attribution,
  `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh`).
- This item covers **uncommitted writes** by the refactor skill. Its commit-time
  guard does not fire (no commit is made), so it needs its own fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The refactor skill refuses to inject finding comments when its target root is
  the main checkout (detected as `git rev-parse --git-dir` ==
  `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, the same rule as the pre-commit guard), and
  reports an actionable message pointing at the worktree requirement.
- Existing behaviour is preserved in a linked worktree and on a feature branch.
- A `git_sandbox` test pins both the refusal (main checkout unchanged, no
  markers written) and the worktree/feature-branch success path.
- Documentation states that refactor must run in a worktree, cross-referencing
  `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.

## Impact

A dispatched refactor session can no longer dirty the shared main checkout,
which today blocks concurrent pre-push gates and worktree creation.
data.title: Refactor skill injects finding comments into the main checkout

# Test: is_main_checkout() unit tests

## Goal

Add unit tests for the shared `is_main_checkout()` utility function in `skill/shared/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Test: `is_main_checkout()` returns `True` in a repo where `.git` is a directory (main checkout).
- Test: `is_main_checkout()` returns `False` in a repo where `.git` is a file pointing to `.git/worktrees/<name>` (worktree).
- Test: `is_main_checkout()` returns `False` when not inside any git repository.
- Test: `is_main_checkout()` correctly distinguishes main checkout from a worktree with a linked `.git` file.
- Tests use `git_sandbox` helpers for repo setup (`init_repo`, `add_worktree`).
- All tests pass with `pytest skill/shared/tests/test_is_main_checkout.py`.
